subject: Availability credits and response SLAs — redline coordination
messages:
From: Tara Lane <tara.lane@layersys.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: legal@layersys.com
Date: 2026-08-05T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Availability and support terms — initial redline

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks for the demo last week. Attached is LayerSys's initial redline of the MSA and Order Form focused on uptime guarantees and support response times. High-level asks:
- 99.9% uptime for Dedicated instances (we rely on this for production workloads)
- Clear severity definitions and 1-hour P1 response SLA
- Service credit cap at 15% of monthly fees
- Prefer 30-day planned maintenance notice and blackout windows during business-critical hours

Please confirm who on your side will own the SLA counters and whether you have an internal playbook for incident credit calculations.

Attaching: LayerSys_Redwood_MSA_Redline.docx

Thanks,

Tara Lane
Head of IT Operations
LayerSys
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Tara Lane <tara.lane@layersys.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-05T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Availability and support terms — initial redline

Tara,

Appreciate the quick turnaround and the redline. I looped in Marcus (sales) and Neha (legal) to triage the asks. Quick responses to your bullets:
- We'll review the 99.9% target; can you share which metrics you use to measure user-impacting downtime?
- We can align on clear severity definitions; Neha will propose preferred language.
- Service credit caps are typically tiered; we'll include our standard escalator for Dedicated vs Hosted.
- Planned maintenance notice: our standard is 72 hours but we can be flexible for longer windows for certain customers.

Next steps: Neha and Marcus will review the redline and propose concrete counterpoints. Can we schedule a 30-min alignment call Thursday or Friday (your timezone)?

Best,

Vanessa Ortiz
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Tara Lane <tara.lane@layersys.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-06T08:29:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Availability and support terms — initial redline

Tara,

Thanks — I've reviewed the redline and propose the following counterpoints to expedite legal review (see inline comments in our draft attached):

1) Uptime targets
- We agree to map Dedicated capacity to a 99.9% monthly availability for the service endpoint that processes inference requests. For Hosted (shared) plans we propose 99.5%.
- Proposal: define "Availability" as successful response within configured latency SLO (e.g., 500ms on p99) to avoid measuring backend infra-only events.

2) Service credits
- We accept a credit mechanism but propose a tiered cap: 5% for a single month for Hosted, 10% for Dedicated, with annual aggregate cap of 30% of monthly recurring fees.
- Credits issued as pro-rata invoice credits applied to the customer's next bill.

3) Response times / Severity
- Severity 1 (production down / data loss): initial response within 1 hour, remediation timeline dependent on incident class; we will provide incident updates per the incident playbook.
- For security incidents, separate incident response commitments apply.

4) Maintenance windows
- We require 72 hours notice for planned maintenance; Redwood will avoid scheduled maintenance during customer's configured business-critical windows when provided.
- Emergency maintenance: Redwood will provide notice as soon as practicable and attempt to schedule outside of critical periods.

5) Auditability
- We will provide monthly availability reports and maintain logs for 90 days unless longer retention is contracted.

I attached a markup (Redwood_SLA_Response_Playbook_v1.pdf) showing concrete language. Marcus — can you confirm procurement constraints on the credit caps and whether a one-time onboarding SLA commitment is required?

Tara — can you confirm if LayerSys will accept invoice credits vs. cash refunds and whether the 30-day maintenance notice is a hard requirement?

Thanks,

Neha Kapoor
Senior Counsel, Commercial Contracts
Redwood Inference
From: Tara Lane <tara.lane@layersys.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: LayerSys Legal <legal@layersys.com>
Date: 2026-08-06T13:57:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Availability and support terms — initial redline

Neha,

Thanks for the clear counterpoints. A few responses from LayerSys:
- Dedicated 99.9% is acceptable; we need an explicit clause that defines how partial outages across zones are treated (i.e., customer-impacting percentage of requests).
- Credits: we prefer a single-month cap of 15% (not tiered) with the ability to escalate to refunds for repeat breaches. Invoice credits are OK but we may request contractual language for refund rights in extraordinary circumstances.
- Maintenance notice: 30 days is preferable for major upgrades; 72 hours acceptable for minor ops but not for changes that affect API compatibility.
- Response times: 1-hour initial response for P1 is non-negotiable for us. We also require 24/7 on-call for P1 with escalation to engineering managers.

We'll be on a call Friday at 10:00 AM PT — does that work for your team? I've attached a short summary page with our expectations.

—
Tara Lane
Head of IT Operations
LayerSys
Attachments: LayerSys_SLA_Summary.pdf
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Tara Lane <tara.lane@layersys.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-07T15:43:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Availability and support terms — initial redline

Tara — thanks. Friday 10:00 AM PT works; I've booked the meeting and included a 30-minute agenda:
1) Finalize uptime metric definition (request vs customer-impact)
2) Agree on credit cap mechanism and remediation steps
3) Confirm maintenance notice windows and emergency handling
4) Next steps & sign-off timeline

Best,
